statedVsRealGaps: roleFamily is tagged 'software_engineering', but this is a real-estate investment / finance role — there is correctly no codebase and no engineering stack; the absence of code is normal, not a defect.

seniorityTarget says 'junior', yet the JD asks for an 'Associate' with 'years of experience in real estate investments' and 'extensive experience closing commercial real estate transactions' — that is a mid-level deal professional, not an entry-level hire. The leveling is internally inconsistent.

The structured 'stack' and 'responsibilities' fields are empty; everything had to be extracted from the JD prose. The prose is rich enough to ground the analysis, so this is a formatting gap, not an evidence gap.

Quantitative thresholds in the JD are blanked/redacted (required years of experience, VC raised, deals identified per week). The precise experience bar and pipeline targets cannot be calibrated from the text.
The JD never names specific systems (Excel is the only tool stated explicitly); CoStar/ARGUS/CRM are inferred from CRE industry norms rather than confirmed.
riskAreas: Mis-leveling: an 'Associate' framed as 'junior' but required to close CRE transactions risks attracting candidates who can model but cannot independently execute deals — or screening out qualified mid-level talent on title alone.

Niche specialization: single-tenant net-lease underwriting (credit-tenant analysis, lease structure, cap-rate dynamics) is narrower than general CRE/IB experience; broad-CRE or pure-IB candidates may lack the STNL-specific skill.

Series A / lean-team context: 'limited oversight', 'reprioritize at a moment's notice', and 'drive projects from planning to completion' demand autonomy and ambiguity-tolerance that a genuine junior won't have — this is an execution role with little mentorship scaffolding.

Investor-facing weighting: IC memos and investor presentations make written/verbal communication and 'simplify complex ideas' as load-bearing as modeling; a modeling-only profile would be underqualified.

Verification limit: with no codebase or independent body of work supplied, every 'real stack' claim is inferred from the JD plus CRE norms — there is no artifact to confirm which tools/systems are actually in use.
analysis.reflection: With no codebase supplied (correct for a real-estate acquisitions role), the 'real body of work' this role acts on is its own materials: Excel underwriting models, lease and property-financial diligence files, market/demographic research, IC memoranda, and investor decks — and the JD describes those richly enough to ground the analysis. The clearest divergence is leveling: the need is tagged junior and software_engineering, but the JD reads as a mid-level real-estate investment Associate expected to underwrite, run full-lifecycle diligence, and help CLOSE single-tenant net-lease deals with limited oversight. Treat the 'software_engineering' family and 'junior' target as metadata errors, not the real shape of the job. In its own terms the work is genuinely complex — complex financial modeling plus multi-workstream due diligence plus investor-facing synthesis — and demands net-lease-specific depth that generic CRE or IB experience may not cover. The main caveats are redacted quantitative thresholds (years, raise, deals/week) and that the toolset beyond Excel is inferred from industry norms rather than stated.

case.title: STNL Acquisition Underwrite & IC Recommendation — Cardinal Pharmacy (Single-Tenant Net-Lease)
case.brief: You are an Acquisitions Associate on a lean acquisitions team. A broker has marketed a single-tenant net-lease (STNL) retail asset leased to Cardinal Pharmacy at an $8,400,000 ask / advertised 6.5% cap. Our Investment Committee meets in 48 hours and wants a recommendation: advance, hold, or reject. The full deal package is below — an offering memorandum (OM), the lease, trailing financials, comps, a lender term sheet, and a partially built Excel model. The provided materials fit this role directly: your job is to underwrite the deal on them, not to build new materials. Two framing notes. First, treat the OM as a sell-side document — reconcile every headline claim to the underlying source documents before you rely on it. Second, our Mandate one-pager states the fund's strategy but is intentionally light on the exact return hurdle, hold period, and exit assumptions; where the package is open, make a defensible call, state it, and move on. Budget ~1.5 hours total — depth on the few decisions that move the recommendation beats exhaustive coverage. Your code/model/memo may be LLM-assisted; what we evaluate is the judgment trail, so the DECISIONS log in Task 4 is part of the deliverable, not optional.
case.repoSeed:
A single-tenant net-lease acquisition package for the Cardinal Pharmacy property:
- OM_CardinalPharmacy.pdf — broker offering memorandum. Headline: $8,400,000 ask, 6.5% cap on 'Year-1 pro-forma rent' of $546,000, '15-year absolute NNN lease, ~9 years remaining', '2% annual rent escalations', 'corporate-guaranteed by Cardinal Pharmacy'.
- Lease_Abstract.xlsx + Lease_CardinalPharmacy.pdf — the actual lease and abstract. Current in-place cash rent $504,000; a 2% bump is scheduled mid-year (the OM annualizes it into the 6.5%). Escalations are CPI-based with a 1% floor / 3% cap (NOT flat 2%). Tenant holds a one-time termination option at the end of Year 6 (≈3 years out) on 12 months' notice with a termination fee of six months' rent. Landlord — not tenant — is responsible for roof and structure. Guaranty is from 'Cardinal Retail Partners LLC', a 42-store franchisee operating company (non-rated), not the Cardinal Pharmacy corporate parent.
- T-12_Operating_Statement.xlsx — trailing-12-month actuals; reported NOI does not tie to the OM's NOI once a management fee and a structural-reserve line are accounted for.
- Rent_Roll.xlsx — single-tenant rent roll with lease dates and current rent.
- STNL_Model.xlsx — partially built underwriting model: DCF, debt-sizing, and IRR/sensitivity tabs scaffolded. The exit-value tab is wired to a rent/NOI cell whose year reference should be checked before use.
- Comps_and_Market.pdf — comparable STNL sales / cap-rate comps and a trade-area demographic snapshot.
- Lender_TermSheet.pdf — debt quote: up to 55% LTV, 6.25% fixed, 30-year amortization, 10-year term, 1.35x DSCR covenant.
- IC_Memo_Template.docx — one-page Investment Committee memo template (recommendation, rationale, risks, conditions).
- Mandate_OnePager.pdf — fund strategy (core-plus STNL, credit-tenant bias) but no pinned return hurdle, hold period, or exit-cap assumption.
tasks: Reconcile the deal basis. Tie the T-12_Operating_Statement.xlsx NOI to the NOI asserted in OM_CardinalPharmacy.pdf, and compute the true in-place going-in cap rate on the $8,400,000 ask using current cash NOI (not the OM's Year-1 pro-forma). Read Lease_Abstract.xlsx / Lease_CardinalPharmacy.pdf against the OM and list every place the lease contradicts the marketing — term, escalations, NNN scope, guarantor. Output a short reconciliation table: OM claim → source-document reality → $ or bps impact.

Underwrite the cash flows in STNL_Model.xlsx. Project levered and unlevered cash flow over the hold you choose, applying the lease's actual CPI escalations (1% floor / 3% cap) and the Lender_TermSheet.pdf debt sized to the lesser of 55% LTV and the 1.35x DSCR covenant. Return unlevered IRR, levered IRR, Year-1 cash-on-cash, and a two-variable sensitivity (exit cap × your chosen swing assumption). State your hold period, exit cap, and return hurdle explicitly — the Mandate one-pager does not pin them down.

Write the IC recommendation (≤1 page, IC_Memo_Template.docx): advance / hold / reject, a 3-sentence transaction rationale a non-modeler can follow, the 2-3 risks that actually swing the decision, and the diligence conditions you'd require before close. Make your treatment of the Year-6 termination option and the franchisee guarantor explicit — surface them, don't bury them.

Keep a DECISIONS log (≤½ page). For every call you made where the package was open — hold period, exit cap, return hurdle, how you treated the termination option, which NOI you underwrote as the basis — note what you chose, the alternative you rejected and why, and the one question you would put to the deal team or broker.

coverProbes.where: Mandate_OnePager.pdf + Task 2 (hold period, exit cap, return hurdle)
coverProbes.reveals: A strong candidate names the hold period, exit-cap assumption, and the return bar they're testing against, ties them to the stated core-plus STNL strategy, and flags that the mandate left them open. A naive candidate silently picks defaults and reports a single IRR as if it were an objective fact, with no hurdle to judge it against.
decisionSpace: Hold to the Year-6 termination-option date (~3y) and underwrite explicit re-leasing / downtime risk past it — conservative, treats the option as the binding horizon.
Hold to lease expiry (~9y) for clean contractual cash flow and a single residual — cleaner IRR but assumes the tenant never exercises the option.
Market-standard 7-10y hold with an exit-cap-expansion haircut over going-in — neutral, but must defend the cap spread.

coverProbes.reveals: A candidate who reads the lease catches the Year-6 termination option, CPI (not flat 2%) escalations, the landlord roof/structure obligation, and the franchisee (not corporate) guaranty. A one-shot modeler inherits the OM's clean '15-year absolute NNN, corporate-guaranteed' story and underwrites a deal that isn't the one in the lease.
decisionSpace: Underwrite to the termination date and treat all post-Year-6 cash flow as speculative re-lease (downtime + TI/LC reserves) — most conservative.
Keep the full term but haircut the residual and carry a structural-reserve line for the landlord roof/structure obligation plus an option reserve — middle path.
Model the termination as a probability-weighted scenario (exercise vs renew) and blend the outcomes — most analytically complete but adds assumption risk.

coverProbes.where: T-12_Operating_Statement.xlsx vs OM cap rate; STNL_Model.xlsx exit-value tab
coverProbes.reveals: A careful candidate reconciles to in-place cash NOI (cap closer to ~6.0% than the advertised 6.5%) and checks that the model's exit value references the correct year's NOI rather than the inflated pro-forma rent. A naive candidate plugs the OM's 6.5% and a great-looking IRR that quietly rests on a rent bump that hasn't hit and a mis-referenced exit cell.
decisionSpace: Underwrite in-place cash NOI as the going-in basis and footnote the pro-forma delta to IC — most defensible basis.
Underwrite the pro-forma rent but only after the contractual bump hits, carrying a reserve for the gap period — acceptable if disclosed.
Present both bases side-by-side and let IC see the bps difference — most transparent, slightly more work.

coverProbes.where: Guaranty entity in the lease vs OM 'corporate-guaranteed'; credit treatment in Tasks 2-3
coverProbes.reveals: A strong candidate flags that the guaranty is a 42-store, non-rated franchisee opco rather than the rated parent, and either adjusts the credit view (store-level rent coverage, wider cap/credit spread) or makes parent financials a condition. A naive candidate accepts 'credit tenant', prices tight, and never tests whether the rent is actually covered.
decisionSpace: Treat as non-credit / operator risk: widen the cap, and require unit-level sales and opco financials before relying on the cash flow.
Make a corporate or parent guaranty (or a lease-level credit enhancement) a closing condition and underwrite to that — pushes risk to the seller.
Accept the franchisee credit but offset with more conservative leverage / a shorter effective underwriting term — keeps the deal alive at a price for risk.
